sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Reimburse the Ikigai Info governance action submitter for a claimed unrecovered governance action deposit plus claimed lost staking rewards.
Recipient: the Ikigai Info governance action submitter / intended recipient, not otherwise named in document
Deliverables: Instant on-chain distribution to the intended recipient upon enactment, No separate administration, audit, or oversight budget; distribution is proposed to be auditable on-chain
Deadline/expiry: Instantly as part of governance action enactment

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal requests 103,000 ADA, consisting of a claimed 100,000 ADA lost deposit plus 3,000 ADA for claimed lost staking rewards at 2% per annum.

Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The proposer says the Ikigai Info governance action submitter could not recover the 100,000 ADA deposit because a Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): The proposal states the original Ikigai action was a symbolic Info governance action thanking contributors and expressing hope for Cardano's future.
Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): The document provides an external reference to an AdaStat page for the referenced governance action.
Claim (adoption, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposer asserts there was significant community sentiment that the Ikigai deposit should be reimbursed.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposer states that entity-based budget submissions did not include this reimbursement after treasury withdrawals became available following the Plomin hard fork.
missing: Independent evidence for: The proposer says the Ikigai Info governance action submitter could not recover the 100,000 ADA deposit because a Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used.
Independent evidence for: The proposer asserts there was significant community sentiment that the Ikigai deposit should be reimbursed.
Independent evidence for: The proposer states that entity-based budget submissions did not include this reimbursement after treasury withdrawals became available following the Plomin hard fork.
Independent evidence for: The proposer states the Cardano in Oceania initiative included the reimbursement in its budget Info governance action, but that action was not approved.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
findings: Six-month treasury flow regime: unknown (stale snapshot) (basis: total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals)
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "The proposal requests 103,000 ADA, consisting of a claimed 100,000 ADA lost deposit plus 3,000 ADA for claimed lost staking rewards at 2% per annum." and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "The proposer says the Ikigai Info governance action submitter could not recover the 100,000 ADA deposit because a Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
